item.description: Israel ordered Britain to close the consulate over sanctions announced on Israeli settlements.

item.content:encoded:
Britain removes East Jerusalem consulate signage as Israeli shutdown deadline expires Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

The British consulate in East Jerusalem seen on Sept 9 (left), and with signage removed on Oct 8. PHOTO: REUTERS

Published   Oct 08, 2026, 02:25 PM

Updated   Oct 08, 2026, 02:28 PM

Set as preferred source

Listen Summarise

Britain removed East Jerusalem consulate signs after Israel’s Oct 8 shutdown deadline expired, worsening already strained ties over West Bank settlement sanctions. Israel ordered the consulate closed and diplomats removed after Britain announced sanctions and a trade ban on goods from Israeli settlements, which most countries call illegal. The closure could affect about 30 diplomats and may prompt Britain to expel Israeli diplomats, a rare move that would deepen the diplomatic row.

AI generated

JERUSALEM - Workers removed signs and plaques at the British consulate in East Jerusalem overnight after Israel ordered it shut by Oct 8 over London’s plans to impose sanctions on settlements in the West Bank , further damaging strained ties between allies. Reuters journalists saw workers in the consulate remove a plaque reading “British Consulate General” and another sign for its consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building. There was no immediate comment from the consulate. Israel ordered Britain in September to close the consulate within 30 days and remove its diplomats from the city, after Britain announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including a trade ban on goods made there.

The United Nations and most countries consider the settlements to be illegal under international law. Israel disputes this. Israel has been adamant the consulate will close even as Britain sought to keep it open, including sending the country’s top national security adviser to Israel last week for talks. Britain’s presence in the city dates back almost 200 years, long before the State of Israel was established in 1948. The closure order does not affect Britain’s embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with Israel’s government.

The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of East Jerusalem, handles Britain’s relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians. Britain’s Foreign Office on Oct 7 declined to comment when asked whether the consulate was still operating or any British diplomats working there had returned to Britain. Sources have said the order to close the consulate affects around 30 British diplomats along with their family members.

Britain is considering expelling Israeli diplomats from its London embassy in response to any closure of the consulate, Reuters reported on Oct 6, citing sources. It would be a highly unusual step for the allies to expel each other’s diplomats. Despite the current strains, Britain and Israel are close economic, security and intelligence partners. The British sanctions announcement, and Israel’s order to close the consulate, mark a new low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years. Britain has repeatedly criticised Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has accused Britain’s governing Labour Party of being hostile towards Israel. REUTERS
